title: Centaurus over the ESO 3.6-metre telescope
caption: Centaurus over the ESO 3.6-metre telescope, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The constellation of Centaurus hangs above the ESO 3.6-metre telescope at La Silla Observatory in Chile's Atacama Desert, set among the crowded stars of the Milky Way. The two bright stars just above the dome are Alpha and Beta Centauri.

Centaurus also contains Proxima Centauri, a red dwarf that is our nearest stellar neighbour. It was the focus of the Pale Red Dot campaign, an international hunt for an Earth-like planet orbiting this nearest of stars that combined science with public outreach.

The search was set to use HARPS, attached to the 3.6-metre telescope seen here, along with BOOTES (the Burst Optical Observer and Transient Exploring System) and the Las Cumbres Observatory Global Telescope Network (LCOGT). The public would be able to watch teams of astronomers with different specialities gather, analyse and interpret data that might, or might not, confirm such a planet.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by A. Santerne. The source does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: The two bright stars above the dome would stand out to the eye too, but a camera gathering light over time records far more of the surrounding Milky Way stars.
